# complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

## 1. Exact overlap law, with arbitrary product-biased data

Let G_T,H_T be real normalized child coefficients; both squared lists have sum one. Let C be their common support, w=sum_C G_T^2=sum_C H_T^2, b=sum_{T in C:G_T=-H_T} G_T^2, and a=1-w. Under OI every common coefficient is equal or opposite; outside C the two exclusive support masses each total a. For F=g at X=0 and h at X=1, independent P(X=1)=p, the parent selector-absent and selector-present masses in residual fiber T are

    A_T=((1-p)G_T+p H_T)^2,
    B_T=p(1-p)(H_T-G_T)^2,
    Q_T=A_T+B_T=(1-p)G_T^2+p H_T^2.

The physical-channel joint masses are (1-p)G_T^2,p H_T^2. Therefore L=M+J by the entropy chain rule, independently of any uncertainty theorem. In a common fiber, the posterior physical probability is p. In an exclusive fiber it is 0 or 1. Thus H(X|T)=w h2(p), and

    J=a h2(p).

On common equal-sign fibers B_T/Q_T=0; on common opposite-sign fibers it is 4p(1-p); on g-only fibers it is p; on h-only fibers it is 1-p. Their Q masses are respectively the common weights, (1-p)a,pa. Consequently

    M=a h2(p)+b h2(4p(1-p)),
    M-J=b h2(4p(1-p))>=0,
    L=2a h2(p)+b h2(4p(1-p)).                 (1)

This repairs J<=M for all interior biases, with no additive tax. At p=1/2, h2(4p(1-p))=h2(1)=0, so M=J=a and L=2a. Parseval gives c=E[gh]=w-2b, hence the actual physical selector influence is

    d=P(g!=h)=(1-c)/2=a/2+b.

Therefore L=2a<=4d, with equality exactly when b=0 (including the zero case). This is a payment of the complete decrement, not only of J. Under biased selector inputs d is still the physical pivotal probability; the biased spectral selector energy is 4p(1-p)d. Formula (1) is not a dimension-independent linear payment by that spectral energy as p tends to zero.

## 2. Terminal-corrected physical tree, influence never reused

At a fair physical split i of any Boolean u, every other coordinate influence is the average of the corresponding child influences, by conditioning the pivotal event on x_i. Hence

    I(u)=Inf_i(u)+(I(u_0)+I(u_1))/2.

For a finite physical tree with node reach weights pi_v, repeated substitution yields sum_v pi_v Inf_{i_v}(u_v)=I(F)-E I(F_leaf). Entropy telescopes on precisely the same tree as H(F)-E H(F_leaf)=sum_v pi_v L_v. OI and (1) imply

    H(F)-E H(F_leaf) <=4 sum_v pi_v Inf_{i_v}(u_v)
                         =4[I(F)-E I(F_leaf)].       (2)

This proves the target and max-constant closure. An irrelevant query has identical children and L=d=0; it incurs no artificial bias tax. If OI fails at some queried nodes, define the actual excess e_v=max(0,L_v-4d_v). The same argument gives the honest version of (2) with +sum_bad pi_v e_v. Bounding that bad-node residual is the remaining universal obligation, not a theorem asserted here.

## 3. Equal-rank quadratic signs, including shared data

Use uniform x in F_2^n. A quadratic sign is f(x)=(-1)^{q(x)}, where q has degree at most two including linear and constant terms. Let B be the polar alternating matrix: q(x+u)+q(x)+q(u)+q(0)=x^T B u, and r=rank(B). Its autocorrelation is

    E_x f(x)f(x+u)=(-1)^{q(u)+q(0)} 1_{u in ker B}.

The phase u->q(u)+q(0) is linear on ker B because its polar form vanishes there. Fourier inversion of the autocorrelation therefore gives fhat(S)^2=2^-r on one affine coset of (ker B)^perp and zero elsewhere. The support has 2^r elements. This proves the flat-spectrum fact for arbitrary n without assuming a literature result.

Any pair of quadratic signs with the same polar rank r has equal nonzero Fourier magnitude 2^(-r/2); it satisfies OI even if affine supports overlap only partly. For an affine support of dimension r, at least r coordinates vary: projection into all varying coordinates is injective, so their count is >=r. Every varying coordinate is fair on that affine support, giving I(f)>=r/2 and H(f)=r<=2 I(f). Thus the selector-first tree has two leaves paid at constant 2; (2) gives H(F)<=4 I(F) on this unbounded shared-data family. Rank zero includes characters and constants.

Strict partial-overlap example: g=(-1)^{y1*y2}, h=(-1)^{y2*y3} on three uniform bits. Both ranks are 2. Their common support is {empty,{y2}}, both common coefficients +1/2, so w=1/2,b=0,d=1/4. The fair selector F has L=1=4d, H(F)=3 and I(F)=5/4. This proves sharpness of local constant 4 while its full H/I is 12/5, not an FEI counterexample.

## 4. Ordered repairs, operations, and exclusions

The tested nested list is R1: distinct characters; R2: disjoint child Fourier supports; R3: OI; R4: unrestricted actual Boolean children. R1 implies R2 implies R3. Both sufficient implications are strict: a constant paired with a balanced fresh-character times a bent function gives disjoint non-character support; the quadratic example above gives partial overlap satisfying R3. R4 fails J<=M on the original biased AND witness. Thus R3 is the weakest sufficient condition in this tested ordered list only. Equal-rank quadratic pairs and isospectral pairs are useful additional subfamilies of R3; neither a global necessity theorem nor a globally weakest hypothesis is claimed.

For an arbitrary independent common Boolean factor k, child coefficients become G_T K_U,H_T K_U. Intersections factor and nonzero common magnitudes remain equal; w,b,d,M,J,L stay unchanged because sum_U K_U^2=1. However terminal entropy gains H(k), and terminal influence gains I(k); (2) retains both. No FEI bound on arbitrary k follows. Multiplying both children by a uniform residual character permutes their spectra, preserves w,b,d, and makes balanced versions if the character is on a fresh bit. Biased coordinate multiplication is not claimed to be a spectral permutation.

For disjoint tensors of admitted pairs, shared supports are products and magnitudes multiply, so OI remains true. For admitted physical trees, process factors one at a time; the other factors are common terminal factors at each query. Influence and entropy add, and leaf constants remain unchanged. For balanced Boolean branches on disjoint physical data blocks, their Fourier supports are disjoint in the full data label space: the only possible intersection is empty, and balancing removes it. Therefore a recursively built fresh-selector hierarchy of disjoint balanced OI modules admits a tree querying outer selectors and then each reached module's selector, with equal-rank quadratic leaves. Balance may be enforced using a fresh common character. Arbitrary depth, module dimension and tensor count are permitted; H<=4I persists. Physical selectors are fresh, and only the data inside each module may be shared.

OI is not closed under arbitrary data restriction. In the partial-overlap example, set y1=0: g becomes constant 1 while h remains a rank-2 quadratic. At their common empty label the magnitudes are 1 and 1/2, violating OI. Consequently we require OI only at actual queried nodes of the chosen tree and do not assert hereditary admission for every tree. Arbitrary weighted thresholds, arbitrary low-energy shared-data multiplexers, all reused-selector circuits, and percolation crossings are not shown to satisfy it. The accepted sparse-bent point-surgery obstruction has typical child g and child g-2 point: its coefficients are generally perturbed in magnitude, so this repair is not an admission proof for that obstruction tree. Blindly declaring it admissible would be the first unsupported line.

## 5. Retain the original obstruction

For biased AND sign 1-2XY with P(X=1)=P(Y=1)=1/4, squared parent masses (empty,X,Y,XY) are (196,12,12,36)/256; the residual Y-present mass is 3/16. The child at X=0 is constant, and the child at X=1 has spectral masses (1/4,3/4), so

    J-M=2 h2(3/16)-H(196,12,12,36 over 256)-(1/4)h2(3/4)>1/16.

The exact rational-log sign is reproduced in out/ORIGINAL_COUNTEREXAMPLE.json. The common empty magnitude is 1 versus 1/2, so the witness violates OI exactly where the repair requires it. Fair residual coordinates and balanced children alone do not repair the claim (A047/A049); common fresh-character balancing preserves that failing common magnitude ratio. In the uniform cube this AND is a harmless flat bent spectrum and does not disprove FEI.

The first unsupported universal line is the existence for every Boolean F of a physical stopping tree whose bad-node excess sum and complete terminal entropy are paid by one dimension-independent influence budget. Equation (2) proves that payment exactly on its declared nodewise hypothesis, not that hypothesis for all functions.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The complete statement and main derivation are CRITICAL_SOURCE_STRUCTURE.tex, equations (1)--(3). Put kappa=2/ln2. For C=A^c, let Y=VS and e0(t)=V_A^-1(y0+V_Ct). Define b=E|S_A+e0(S_C)| and epsilon=P(Y!=y0). The physical Hamming weight gives b<=r epsilon. The partial Fourier channel v_t(x)=sum_e fhat(e,t)chi_e(x) has child probabilities v_t(x)^2, whose mean is the S_C marginal. Hence

    L_A=H(S_A|S_C)+J_A=H(Y|S_C)+J_A.

For each t, multiply v_t by chi_e0(t). This leaves its square unchanged and shifts its Fourier labels by e0(t). Logarithmic Sobolev applied to the absolute value of this real function gives

    (ln2) J_A=sum_t Ent(v_t^2)
        <=2 sum_(e,t) |e+e0(t)| fhat(e,t)^2 = 2b.

Here is a self-contained justification of the analytic inequality used. For a nonnegative two-point function (u,v), homogeneity and symmetry reduce to (t,1), t>=1. Twice the difference between the desired Dirichlet bound and Ent is

    F(t)=(t^2+1)ln((t^2+1)/2)-2t^2 ln t+(t-1)^2.

F(1)=0 and F'(t)=2t ln((t^2+1)/(2t^2))+2(t-1). The difference 1-1/t-ln(2t^2/(t^2+1)) vanishes at one and has derivative (t-1)^2/[t^2(t^2+1)]>=0. Thus F'>=0. Symmetry F(t)=t^2 F(1/t) and continuity handle the remaining values. Entropy tensorization then proves Ent(w^2)<=1/2 sum_i E(|w(x)|-|w(x+e_i)|)^2<=2 sum_i ||D_i w||_2^2 for real w on a uniform product cube. Tensorization follows inductively by conditioning and convexity of Ent; no biased inequality is imported. Parseval after each fiber's character shift yields the displayed 2b. Zero marginal fibers vanish identically.

Criticality is used only in the physical-child deficit comparison:

    L_A-R(f)I_A=-E[H(f_x)-R(f)I(f_x)]>=0.

Consequently R(f)I_A<=H(Y|S_C)+kappa b. In the threshold-critical form the left side is KI_A+D_K(f). Since H(Y)<=h2(epsilon)+epsilon log2(2^r-1), the explicit concentration obstruction is

    KI_A+D_K(f) <= h2(epsilon)
        +epsilon log2(2^r-1)+kappa r epsilon.

For a nonempty flip mask u and a pivot i in its support, r=1, b=epsilon_u, where epsilon_u=(1-|E f(x)f(x+u)|)/2. Thus KI_i+D_K(f)<=h2(epsilon_u)+kappa epsilon_u. In particular a positive-entropy ratio-critical source in essential coordinates has no exact signed translation symmetry. This strengthens the exact-symmetry removal baseline quantitatively, without a uniform positive lower bound when influence vanishes.

PRUNING_SCOPE.md replays both historical failures, checks their higher-ratio physical restrictions in the inherited indicator orientation, and separately certifies that both sign lifts have actual point-defect descendants with ratio more than 1/2 larger. Components are never assumed to be descendants. Arbitrary-core activation remains FEI-hard as a class, but its amplified K-violations contain smaller K-violating physical cores and fail dimension minimality. Descendants are not assumed critical. The reviewed raw-AND-power degree-moment obstruction is retained at its distinct scope.

First unsupported line: for some absolute finite K, every prospective dimension-critical K-witness admits a proper physical pivot block with H(VS|S_C)+kappa b<=KI_A. Such a block would contradict the strictly positive deficit. The present result supplies a necessary spectral-disorder restriction and a sufficient certificate for extracting a better child; it does not prove that an affordable block exists universally or pay component excess.

# complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

With p=2^-n and g=f-2f(a)1_a, the exact influence change is 2p sum_i f(a)f(a^i). Additive mixed derivative energy changes by p(r_i+r_j-r_ij), while multiplicative plaquette probability changes by 4p sigma_ij(a). Across a product cut the latter is exactly 4p and centered spectral covariance has absolute value <=7p+4p^2. Raw additive mixed-derivative positivity is not a nonfactorization statistic.

Vanishing cross-cut plaquettes are equivalent to coordinate tensor factorization. A one-point flip of a nontrivial product changes the whole-cube product from +1 to -1, ruling out every nontrivial coordinate factorization. All integer Walsh sums are then 2 mod4, proving full support. These are exact conditions, not visual circuit connectedness.

For n>=4, |H(g)-H(f)|<=h2(u_n)+n u_n, u_n=2^(1-floor(n/2)); influence error is <=2np. Both estimates are uniform in tensor count, core dimensions and point location and include zero old coefficients.

For any fixed nonconstant d-bit core h, balanced powers F_t=z*h^tensor t have H=tH(h), I=tI(h)+1. Their one-point surgeries G_t are tensor-prime, full-support, all-essential and have connected plaquette graphs, yet H(G_t)/I(G_t) tends to H(h)/I(h). Across the fresh-sign cut the total plaquette curvature is 4td*2^(-td-1), tending to zero, and the corresponding summed absolute covariance also tends to zero. The simultaneous qualitative class therefore has the same extended optimal FEI constant as unrestricted Boolean signs. This is an admission equivalence, not an actual unbounded-ratio family.

For t>=2 fixing another copy away from its surgery coordinates removes the defect and leaves +/-h as a proper physical descendant. Thus a strict violating core makes these admitted embeddings fail dimension-criticality. A051's stronger all-descendant tests remain distinct and useful.

# A056: balanced disjoint substitution and its physical restrictions

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

For every finite k and pairwise disjoint physical coordinate blocks B_i, let g_i:{-1,1}^{B_i}->{-1,1}, let h:{-1,1}^k->{-1,1}, and put F=h(g_1,...,g_k). Physical coordinates are independent uniform signs. Entropy H is Shannon entropy in bits of the **entire** squared Fourier spectrum, including the empty coefficient; I is expected Fourier-set size, equivalently total flip influence. No restriction on the mean of h is needed. First assume every g_i is balanced: E g_i=0. Then

    E F = E h,
    Var F = Var h,
    H(F) = H(h) + sum_i Inf_i(h) H(g_i),
    I(F) = sum_i Inf_i(h) I(g_i),
    Inf_x(F) = Inf_i(h) Inf_x(g_i),  x in B_i.

This packet proves these identities, extends them to arbitrary child means, and identifies precisely what must be updated after a physical restriction. These are composition baseline identities, not a proof of unrestricted FEI. The complete analytic proof is local; independent acceptance is pending.

## sources actually read, revisions and theorem locators

Execution protocol revision 2026-10-11-execution-v2 governs this run. Campaign README, CURRENT_STATUS, claim/obstruction/packet registries, STREAM_NEXT_ACTIONS, the LaTeX plan and earlier B05/B09/B19 reports were inspected for scope and review guards. The advisory campaign CAMPAIGN, CLAIMS, COUNTEREXAMPLES, SEED_LEMMAS, NATIVE_MAPPING and source archive supply route context. Exact filenames and byte hashes are recorded in out/source_manifest.json; mathematical source excerpts are in out/source_excerpts.txt.

The threshold 38-page local text, Section 7, Proposition 7.1, equations (67)-(70), contains exact product-measure strong-entropy, influence and deficit identities. Section 7.3, Corollary 7.8, specializes to balanced children. Section 6.1 defines the strong entropy and product Fourier basis; these must not be confused with ordinary full Shannon entropy. Its earlier 29-page version and both percolation text versions were inspected for normalization/context. The percolation 30-page text Section 1.1 uses normalized product characters; its geometric hypotheses supply no premise to this proof. ## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### Balanced coefficient identity

Write g_i=sum_{U subset B_i} c_i(U) chi_U and h=sum_{T subset [k]} a(T) chi_T. Balance means c_i(empty)=0. For a physical Fourier set S, put S_i=S intersect B_i and T(S)={i:S_i is nonempty}. Expanding h after substitution, a term indexed by T can contribute to S only if T=T(S): unused blocks contribute the constant 1, and every used block has a nonempty set. Disjoint blocks make the union unique. Hence, including S=empty,

    Fhat(S) = a(T(S)) product_{i in T(S)} c_i(S_i).                  (1)

Parseval gives sum_{U nonempty} c_i(U)^2=1. Thus the spectral law is exactly the following experiment: sample T with probability a(T)^2; independently for each i in T sample a nonempty U_i with probability c_i(U_i)^2; output S=union U_i. Conversely S recovers T and every U_i. The experiment is bijective on positive-probability outcomes, so its entropy is H(h)+sum_i P(i in T)H(g_i). Since P(i in T)=Inf_i(h), this proves the entropy formula, with no latent-label correction or omitted empty atom. Its expected size is sum_i Inf_i(h)I(g_i). The probability a given x in B_i is included is Inf_i(h)Inf_x(g_i). Finally (1) at empty proves E F=E h and therefore the variance formula. Zero coefficients are simply omitted; 0 log(1/0)=0.

### Arbitrary means: reexpanded outer gate

Let m_i=E g_i and v_i=1-m_i^2. First absorb all deterministic children (v_i=0) into h by fixing those output coordinates to m_i. This is exact because a Boolean uniform-cube function of mean +/-1 is constant at every input. Reindex the remaining children; now v_i>0. Their independent output law is mu, with P(Y_i=+1)=(1+m_i)/2. In its orthonormal basis psi_i(y)=(y_i-m_i)/sqrt(v_i), write

    h(y)=sum_T a_mu(T) product_{i in T} psi_i(y).

Define P_mu(T)=a_mu(T)^2, w_i=sum_{T containing i} P_mu(T), H_mu(h)=H(P_mu), and I_mu(h)=sum_T |T|P_mu(T). These biased spectral influences w_i are not the ordinary unweighted pivotal probabilities. Indeed w_i=v_i E_mu[(D_i h)^2], where D_i h=(h(y_i=+1)-h(y_i=-1))/2 on the other outputs.

On the physical block,

    (g_i-m_i)/sqrt(v_i)=sum_{U nonempty} c_i(U)/sqrt(v_i) chi_U.

This again has zero empty coefficient and squared mass one. The same unique union argument gives

    Fhat(S)=a_mu(T(S)) product_{i in T(S)} c_i(S_i)/sqrt(v_i).       (2)

The child's nonempty spectral law is q_i(U)=c_i(U)^2/v_i. Its entropy K_i satisfies

    H(g_i)=h2(v_i)+v_i K_i,                                        (3)

because the empty atom has mass m_i^2=1-v_i. The exact full identities are consequently

    E F = E_mu h = a_mu(empty),       Var F=Var_mu h,
    H(F)=H_mu(h)+sum_i (w_i/v_i)[H(g_i)-h2(v_i)],                   (4)
    I(F)=sum_i (w_i/v_i) I(g_i),
    Inf_x(F)=(w_i/v_i)Inf_x(g_i), x in B_i.                        (5)

Equations (2)-(5) are valid at every finite dimension, for arbitrary nonconstant child means. All entropy terms are finite; no limiting assertion is needed. If every child was deterministic, F is constant and all entropies and influences are zero. Outer irrelevant coordinates have w_i=0 and require no child contribution. Balanced children give v_i=1, h2(v_i)=0 and the uniform outer law, recovering the first formulas.

For comparison with Proposition 7.1, the strong-entropy convention must be distinguished from conditional nonempty entropy. The convention that actually composes is Eplus(g)=sum_{U nonempty} c(U)^2 log2(1/c(U)^2) on uniform physical inputs, and Eplus_mu(h)=sum_{T nonempty} P_mu(T)log2(product v_i/P_mu(T)) on outputs. Then exactly

    Eplus(F)=Eplus_mu(h)+sum_i (w_i/v_i) Eplus(g_i).                (6)

It follows immediately from (2), with no Var(F) numerator. The conditional nonempty entropy in (3), namely H(g)-h2(Var(g)), is a different quantity. This run's main identities (1)-(5) deliberately use full H or conditional K, so do not depend on a strong-entropy naming convention. Define deficit delta=I-Var. Since sum_i w_i=I_mu(h), and Var(F)=Var_mu(h),

    delta(F)=delta_mu(h)+sum_i (w_i/v_i)delta(g_i).                 (7)

### Physical restrictions: what survives, and what changes

Fix actual physical coordinates W to a deterministic assignment rho. In each block replace g_i by g_i^rho=g_i restricted to W intersect B_i. Remaining inputs retain the independent uniform law and disjoint supports. Therefore (2)-(5) hold with the **new** means m_i^rho, variances v_i^rho, absorbed deterministic children, and the Fourier expansion of the reduced outer gate under the **new** output product law. They do not generally hold with old a_mu or old w_i. The balanced formulas are available at a reached branch when every remaining nonconstant child is balanced after absorption of constants. If only one child is restricted, all untouched initially balanced children remain balanced, but the changed child must be checked. Balance of that child is sufficient; it is not claimed logically necessary for accidental numerical equality in a special gate.

For a single initially balanced child j, write the uniform outer polynomial as h=A(y_-j)+y_j B(y_-j). Let a_T=Ahat(T), b_T=Bhat(T), and let the changed child's mean be m, variance v=1-m^2>0. Other children stay balanced. Recenter:

    h=A+mB+sqrt(v) psi_j B.

The new outer coefficients are a_T+m b_T on T not containing j, and sqrt(v)b_T on T union {j}. Thus squared weights include the coherent term 2m a_T b_T; they cannot be replaced by separate a_T^2 and m^2 b_T^2. Direct physical coefficients are (a_T+m b_T) product_{i in T} c_i(S_i) when S_j is empty, and b_T c_j^rho(S_j) product_{i in T} c_i(S_i) otherwise. The j-block physical multiplier is still sum_T b_T^2=Inf_j(h), because w_j^rho=v sum_T b_T^2. Other block multipliers generally change.

If v=0, fix outer y_j=m, giving the actual reduced polynomial A+mB. Do not divide by v. If m=0, the original outer coefficients remain valid. If the restriction is chosen adaptively using already observed physical values, each fixed leaf of the physical decision tree is a cylinder and its unrevealed coordinates are independent uniform. The formulas apply branchwise. An expectation over leaves must retain the branch-specific outer laws and weights; it cannot silently substitute the initial gate's spectrum. Conditioning only on a child output instead of fixing physical coordinates is not such a cylinder and need not leave a product physical law.

### Exact witness against retaining the old balanced formulas

Let h(y,z)=AND_2(y,z) in sign notation: +1 only when both inputs are +1. Its uniform spectrum has four coefficients of magnitude 1/2, so E h=-1/2, H(h)=2, and Inf_y(h)=Inf_z(h)=1/2. Let the first initially balanced child be majority on three signs (x,a,b), and the second be a fresh dictator z. Physically fixing x=+1 changes the first child to OR_2(a,b), with mean 1/2, variance 3/4, H=2 and I=1. The restricted F=AND_2(OR_2(a,b),z) has constant coefficient -1/4, z coefficient 3/4, and the other six coefficients of magnitude 1/4. Its spectrum is seven atoms 1/16 and one atom 9/16. Hence

    E F=-1/4,     I(F)=5/4,
    H(F)=4-(9/16)log2(9)=4-(9/8)log2(3).

Retaining old balanced formulas predicts E F=-1/2, I(F)=1, H(F)=3. All three predictions are false. For the entropy comparison, 3 > H(F) follows exactly from 3^9>2^8, with no floating point. The new output-biased gate weights are 1/16, 3/16, 9/16, 3/16 on empty, {y}, {z}, {y,z}. Thus w_y=3/8 and w_z=3/4, and (5) gives (3/8)/(3/4)+(3/4)=5/4. This is an actual Boolean physical restriction of an initially balanced substitution, not an arbitrary spectral law.

### Scope of consequences

Ordinary bounds H(h)<=C I(h) and H(g_i)<=C I(g_i) alone do not give the same C under the balanced identity: the outer H(h) remains an additional term. A sufficient balanced compositional invariant is H(q)<=C[I(q)-Var(q)] for the gate and all children. Since Var(g_i)=1, the formulas give H(F)<=C[I(F)-Var(F)]. This is a conditional consequence of explicitly stated gate/child bounds; those bounds are not proved for arbitrary Boolean functions here. After a physical restriction, either verify balance again or use product-biased identities and gate hypotheses at the new means. An arbitrary weighted threshold theorem established only for uniform inputs cannot be applied at newly biased child outputs. No overlap theorem, selector credit, or full FEI conclusion follows from these identities alone.

There is no unsupported line in the proofs of (1)-(5), (6)-(7), or the witness. General dimension-independent FEI remains open. The unpaid next research term is a quantitative entropy/influence payment for changed biased gate laws or overlapping-block coherent coefficients; it is not supplied by disjoint identities.

# A056 stage 2: biased-child erasure and physical entropy decrement

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Pair functionals and the exact coordinate identity

Define phi(s)=s log2(1/s) for s>0, phi(0)=0, and

    e(s,t)=phi(s)+phi(t)-phi(s+t),
    d(a,b)=phi(a^2)+phi(b^2)-[phi((a+b)^2)+phi((a-b)^2)]/2,
    j(a,b)=d(a,b)-e(a^2,b^2).

All three relevant functions are homogeneous of degree one in squared amplitudes: e(cs,ct)=c e(s,t), and d(sqrt(c)a,sqrt(c)b)=c d(a,b), likewise j. In particular e(s,t)=(s+t)h2(t/(s+t)), and

    j(a,b)=(a^2+b^2)[1-h2(1/2+ab/(a^2+b^2))] >= 0.             (1)

For a physical Fourier pair a_U=fhat(U), b_U=fhat(U union {i}), where U excludes i,

    B_i(f)=sum_U e(a_U^2,b_U^2),
    D_i(f)=sum_U d(a_U,b_U),
    JS_i(f)=D_i(f)-B_i(f)=sum_U j(a_U,b_U).                       (2)

Indeed restriction replaces the pair by a_U+b_U or a_U-b_U. The average pair mass equals a_U^2+b_U^2, so subtracting the raw entropies proves (2), without normalization or omitted empty pair. Formulas (1)-(2) apply even if a pair has zero mass.

### 2. Recentered outer coefficients and exact biased splits

Write h(y)=A(y_-j)+y_j B(y_-j). Expand A and B in the **normalized product basis of the other child outputs under their current means**, not necessarily under the uniform output law. Let their coefficients be a_T,b_T. For the chosen child, put

    m=E g_j, v=1-m^2, beta=g_jhat({i}), t=beta^2,
    C_T=a_T+m b_T, q=sum_T b_T^2=E[B(Y_-j)^2].

Since h is Boolean, B is 0 or +/-1 and q is its pivotal probability under the other outputs. For v>0 the recentered outer coefficients are C_T and sqrt(v)b_T; its biased spectral j-inclusion is w_j=vq. The physical multiplier is q, including when other children are biased. The actual influence identity is

    Inf_i(F)=q Inf_i(g_j).                                      (3)

Define the positive outer functions

    M(t)=sum_T e(C_T^2,t b_T^2),
    N(t)=sum_T j(C_T,beta b_T).

N depends only on beta^2, since j is even in either amplitude. Define the child's residual sectors, with precisely its empty i-deleted pair removed,

    B_i^*(g_j)=B_i(g_j)-e(m^2,t),
    D_i^*(g_j)=D_i(g_j)-d(m,beta).

Both are nonnegative, as sums of the nonempty U sectors in (2). Then the exact identities are

    B_i(F)=q B_i^*(g_j)+M(t),                                   (4)
    D_i(F)=q D_i^*(g_j)+M(t)+N(t).                              (5)

Equivalently, define signed corrections

    L_m(t)=M(t)-q e(m^2,t),
    K_m(t)=N(t)-q j(m,beta).

Then

    B_i(F)=q B_i(g_j)+L_m(t),
    D_i(F)=q D_i(g_j)+L_m(t)+K_m(t).                            (6)

Proof: for a nonempty selected-child Fourier set U, both coordinate-pair amplitudes have multiplier b_T, times the normalized nonempty spectra of occupied other child blocks. Homogeneity and Parseval on those child laws give q times the corresponding child pair contribution. For U=empty, the no-i amplitude is C_T, while the with-i amplitude is beta b_T. Parseval eliminates the other-block factors, giving M or M+N. The physical union identifies T and each other child's nonempty set, so no two distinct outer terms are squared incoherently. This also proves (3). Signed recentering is carried by C_T=a_T+m b_T throughout.

When m=0, e(m^2,t)=j(m,beta)=0, so (6) reduces to A057's balanced identity. When t=0, M=N=0 and the selected empty pair contributes nothing. When v=0, the child is constant, beta=0, its B/D and every query influence are zero; fix the gate coordinate and do not divide by v. Irrelevant gates have q=0 and all terms vanish. These statements cover every endpoint.

### 3. Positive-sector envelope valid at biased descendants

For v>0, Parseval gives 0<=t<=v. As a function of s>=0, M(s) is nonnegative, nondecreasing, concave, and M(0)=0. Each e(C^2,s b^2) has derivative b^2 log2(1+C^2/(s b^2)) when s b^2>0; its second derivative is nonpositive, with zero-amplitude cases handled by continuity. At s=v,

    M(v)=B_j^mu(h),                                            (7)

where B_j^mu means coordinate erasure of the **normalized biased outer squared spectrum**. This is a spectral conditional entropy, not the erasure under a uniform outer law and not a pivotal probability.

Set theta=t/v. Concavity of phi yields, term by term,

    M(t) <= theta M(v)+q t log2(v/t),
    M(t) <= M(v).

Thus, with t log(v/t)=0 when t=0,

    M(t) <= min{B_j^mu(h),
                 (t/v) B_j^mu(h)+q t log2(v/t)}.                (8)

To check the first inequality explicitly, phi(C^2+theta v b^2)>=(1-theta)phi(C^2)+theta phi(C^2+v b^2), while phi(theta v b^2)=theta phi(v b^2)+theta v b^2 log2(1/theta). Sum the resulting e inequality. No positivity of the signed L_m or K_m is assumed; the envelope applies to M.

The one-bit logarithmic Sobolev inequality gives

    0<=N(t)<= (2/ln 2) sum_T min(C_T^2,t b_T^2)
             <= (2/ln 2)q t.                                  (9)

Here is a self-contained scalar proof of the inequality used. For x>=y>=0, Ent_uniform((x^2,y^2)) in nats is at most (x-y)^2/2. By homogeneity take y=1. The difference F(x) between this upper bound and the entropy satisfies F(1)=F'(1)=F''(1)=0 and F'''(x)=2(x^2-1)/(x(x^2+1)^2)>=0; integrate three times for x>=1. The y=0 endpoint follows by continuity. Apply it to x=|a+b|, y=|a-b| (interchange if needed); their squared difference is 4 min(a^2,b^2). Division by ln2 proves j(a,b)<=2 min(a^2,b^2)/ln2. This proves (9), independently of an unreviewed imported estimate.

Combining (5),(8),(9) gives the exact positive-sector interface with the outer logarithmic remainder retained. In particular D_i(F) is bounded by q D_i^*(g_j) plus the right-hand side of (8) plus (2/ln2)qt.

### 4. What is paid once in a physical stopping tree

The Boolean derivative takes values 0,+/-1, so |beta|=|E D_i g_j|<=E[(D_i g_j)^2]=Inf_i(g_j). Since v<=1,

    q t log2(v/t) <= q t log2(1/t)
                   <= [2/(e ln2)] q |beta|
                   <= [2/(e ln2)] Inf_i(F).                    (10)

The scalar middle bound maximizes u ln(1/u) at u=1/e. Also qt<=Inf_i(F), so (9) costs at most (2/ln2)Inf_i(F). At every node of an adaptive **physical** restriction tree, the remaining blocks stay disjoint and the unrevealed physical signs stay independent uniform; recompute all child means and the current other-output basis. Therefore these two components have cumulative expected price at most

    [(2+2/e)/ln2] [I(root)-E I(leaf)].                          (11)

This uses the physical-query influence telescope once. It does not recharge a whole-subformula bank at each depth. Formula (11) pays only the explicit logarithm and outer JS component; it does not pay q D_i^*(child), the capped biased outer-erasure terms, or terminal entropy.

### 5. Restriction control and a signed-correction obstruction

For the required AND2(Maj3(x,a,b),z) control, first fix x=+1. The selected child is OR2(a,b) with m=1/2, v=3/4, beta=1/2 at either a or b. The other child is a fresh dictator. The recentered gate has C_empty=-1/4, C_{z}=3/4 and b_empty=b_{z}=1/2, so q=1/2. Equations (4)-(6) retain the child's nonzero empty pair e(1/4,1/4)=1/2 and d(1/2,1/2)=1. Its full B_i is 1 and D_i is 2, hence B_i^*=1/2 and D_i^*=1. Independently restricting a gives a dictator z at a=+1 (H=0), and AND2(b,z) at a=-1 (H=2). Thus

    D_a(F)=H(F)-1=3-(9/8)log2(3),
    Inf_a(F)=1/4,
    B_a(F)=1/4+M(1/4).

The exact coefficients and prime-log vectors are saved in out/checks.json. The total influence of this restricted F remains 5/4, as adopted in stage 1.

Signed corrections need not be nonnegative at biased descendants. Take h=AND2 and both children OR2 on disjoint two-bit blocks. For a selected coordinate of the first child, m=1/2, beta=1/2, q=3/4; the other child has mean 1/2 and variance 3/4. The signed erasure correction is

    L_m(1/4)= 1/4-(9/8)log2(3)+(5/8)log2(5)<0.                (12)

Indeed (12) is negative exactly when 4*5^5<3^9 (12500<19683), an integer comparison. The same fixture has K_m(1/4)=5/4-(5/8)log2(5)=(5/8)log2(4/5)<0, certified simply by 4<5. This directly prevents silently applying the balanced nonnegative-L/JS bank to biased children. The positive M,N envelope remains valid. The finite census records 512 negative L and 512 negative K cases; their exact signs use integer products, never decimals. These are scope controls inside the same interface extension, not additional broad candidate claims.

### 6. Honest first unsupported line

For a represented physical stopping tree, the unproved universal line is a dimension-independent bound on

    E H(leaf) + E sum_visited [q_v D_{i_v}^*(g_{v,j_v})
                 + min{B_{j_v}^{mu_v}(h_v),
                       (beta_v^2/v_v) B_{j_v}^{mu_v}(h_v)}]

by K I(root), with any legitimate allocation of the paid logarithmic terms and without repeatedly spending the same influence or dropping the negative empty-sector credit. Our estimates justify such a residual target but do not prove it. The displayed min is the smaller gate-only part after applying the two alternative bounds; a proof must couple that choice with the associated logarithmic bill. Using min of gate parts and paying the logarithm regardless is a valid upper bound. Arbitrary terminal child entropy remains present, so admission of an arbitrary hard core has not been bypassed.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The complete proof is COHERENT_REMAINDER_PAYMENT.tex. Here is its mathematical ledger.

1. Put A_T=a_T^2, B_T=b_T^2, s_T=A_T+xB_T. The exact remainder is L_j(x)+J_j(x), where L_j(x)=sum s_T h_nat(x B_T/s_T) and J_j(x)=E(s)-[Eraw(a+alpha b)+Eraw(a-alpha b)]/2. Orthogonality gives identical total squared mass M=1-q+qx for both coherent child vectors. Thus J is a raw equal-mass JS divergence, not an entropy of an admitted Boolean leaf.
2. The actual erasure identity is B_i(F)=q B_i(h_j)+L_j(x). Residual block-j nonempty sectors contribute q times the inner erasure; the empty block-j sector has masses A_T,xB_T and contributes L. The corresponding JS identity is JS_i(F)=q JS_i(h_j)+J_j(x). These formulas retain the coherent phase dependence of physical child spectra.
3. Concavity of -u ln u gives E(A+xB)>=(1-x)E(A)+xE(A+B), hence L_j(x)<=x B_j(g)+qx ln(1/x). JS-Hellinger gives J_j(x)<=2 sum min(A_T,xB_T)<=2qx. Therefore R<=x B_j(g)+qx ln(1/x)+2qx. Every zero and endpoint case is covered in the proof.
4. Boolean physical half-differences give |alpha|<=Inf_i(h_j). Calculus yields alpha^2 ln(1/alpha^2)<=(2/e)|alpha|. Since Inf_i(F)=q Inf_i(h_j), the explicit logarithm costs at most (2/e) Inf_i(F). The constant in bits is 2/(e ln2), about 1.0615; the proof uses its exact symbolic value. This is a payment in actual influence, not an O(alpha^2) replacement.
5. Any finite actual physical restriction tree has I(f)=sum_internal w_v Inf_{i_v}(f_v)+E I(leaf). Thus the logarithmic bank over represented nodes costs at most (2/e) I(f), without reusing the same physical query. Full remainder sum is at most sum w_v alpha_v^2 B_{j_v}(g_v)+(2+2/e) consumed influence. Nodes need certified balanced representations; biased descendants are not assumed to retain them.
6. At a single root, sum over physical coordinates to get B(F)<=sum_j q_j B(h_j)+sum_j W_1(h_j) B_j(g)+(2/e)I(F). This is an exact interface to outer erasure transport, not a depth-independent recursive closure.

# A061: fair adaptive restriction entropy process

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

For every n>=0 and Boolean sign f on the uniform cube, construct its entropy process along any finite fair adaptive physical restriction tree. Entropy uses bits, I is ordinary total influence. Prove exact conditional increments and the stopped tree identity, retaining terminal entropy. Identify the sign and a proved sufficient hypothesis for a compensated supermartingale. Full FEI remains OPEN. This is an A061 baseline/interface completion, not a claim of novelty or a universal payment theorem.

Context source hashes and precise inspection record are in out/SOURCE_RECEIPTS.json when the metadata job completes.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Probability space and filtration

Sample X uniformly from {-1,1}^n. For randomized policies, also sample an independent policy seed R at time zero. Let F_t contain R, all coordinates queried before t and their physical values. The next coordinate i_t and the decision to stop must be F_t-measurable. Never query a coordinate twice. Conditional on F_t and continuation, X_i_t is a fair sign, and the remaining unqueried coordinates are uniform and independent. This follows inductively because a policy uses only revealed values and its independent seed. Let g_t be the actual Boolean function obtained by restricting f to the observed assignment. Let tau<=n be the stopping time. Freeze g_t and all processes after tau; all increments and charges below are zero there.

Write E_t=H(g_t), V_t=I(g_t), d_t=Inf_i_t(g_t). At a live node suppress t. Let a_T=ghat(T) and b_T=ghat(T union {i}) for T not containing i. Set q_T=a_T^2+b_T^2, theta_T=b_T^2/q_T on q_T>0. The child Fourier coefficients are a_T+sigma b_T, sigma in {+1,-1}. Let p_sigma(T)=(a_T+sigma b_T)^2. Boolean Parseval makes each p_sigma a probability law; their fair average is q. Thus d=sum b_T^2=sum q_T theta_T.

The spectral probabilities q_T and theta_T are not physical branch probabilities. At this one node one may introduce a fresh auxiliary experiment: sample sigma fairly, then Y with law p_sigma. It has marginal q, and J=I(sigma;Y)=H(q)-[H(p_+)+H(p_-)]/2. No global spectral subset is assumed to undergo the physical restriction.

### 2. Exact one-step increments

Let B=sum_T q_T h_2(theta_T), J as above, D=B+J. Splitting the parent spectral law into the removed bit and T gives H(g)=H(q)+B. Therefore

    D = H(g) - (H(g_+)+H(g_-))/2 >= 0.

Let eta_H=(H(g_+)-H(g_-))/2 and eta_I=(I(g_+)-I(g_-))/2. The exact realized increments, with sigma=X_i, are

    E_{t+1}-E_t = -D_t + sigma eta_H,t,
    V_{t+1}-V_t = -d_t + sigma eta_I,t.

For the influence identity, the average squared child coefficient at T is q_T, so average child influence is sum |T|q_T. Parent influence is that sum plus sum b_T^2. Fairness kills the sigma terms conditionally. In particular E_t and V_t are supermartingales; neither need decrease on every physical branch.

Define A_t=sum_{s<t}D_s and P_t=sum_{s<t}d_s (stopped charges). Then E_t+A_t and V_t+P_t are martingales. Their initial values are H(f) and I(f). They are integrable: 0<=E_t<=n, 0<=V_t<=n, 0<=D_t<=n, 0<=d_t<=1, and tau<=n. Summing finitely many conditional expectations gives

    H(f)=E H(g_tau)+E sum_{t<tau}D_t,
    I(f)=E I(g_tau)+E sum_{t<tau}d_t.

For a deterministic tree with node reach probability pi_v=2^{-depth(v)}, these are exactly H(f)=sum_internal pi_v D_v+sum_leaf pi_l H(g_l) and I(f)=sum_internal pi_v d_v+sum_leaf pi_l I(g_l). A randomized policy averages these identities over its seed. Terminal entropy cannot be dropped unless the leaves have zero entropy or it has a separate bound. Constant leaves have H=I=0; a terminal character can have H=0 and I>0.

### 3. A proved logarithmic compensation

Define the nonnegative predictable one-sided log charge

    lambda_t=sum_{T:b_T^2>0} b_T^2 log_2(q_T/b_T^2).

For theta in [0,1], -(1-theta)ln(1-theta)<=theta, since the derivative of theta+(1-theta)ln(1-theta) is -ln(1-theta)>=0. Consequently B_t<=lambda_t+d_t/ln 2.

Here is a self-contained channel bound. Put z=|2ab|/q in [0,1] for a positive packet. Its JS contribution is q d_nat(z)/ln 2, where d_nat(z)=((1+z)ln(1+z)+(1-z)ln(1-z))/2. The inequality d_nat(z)<=1-sqrt(1-z^2) holds: the derivatives are atanh(z) and z/sqrt(1-z^2), and the latter minus the former has derivative (1-z^2)^(-3/2)-(1-z^2)^(-1)>=0 and starts at zero. Integrate twice and extend to z=1 by continuity. Therefore the packet contribution is at most (q-|a^2-b^2|)/ln 2=2min(a^2,b^2)/ln 2. Summation gives J_t<=2d_t/ln 2. Combining,

    0<=D_t<=lambda_t+(3/ln 2)d_t.                 (* proved *)

Thus the explicit compensated quantity

    U_t=(3/ln 2)V_t-E_t-sum_{s<t}lambda_s

is ALWAYS a supermartingale on the stated finite trees: its conditional drift is D_t-(3/ln 2)d_t-lambda_t<=0. It is integrable: every nonzero Fourier coefficient of an actual restriction in at most n coordinates has magnitude at least 2^{-n}, q_T<=1, so every positive theta_T>=2^{-2n} and lambda_t<=2n d_t. The log cost is paid once, through its predictable cumulative sum. At stopping this yields only

    H(f)<= (3/ln 2)I(f) + E sum lambda_t
           + E[H(g_tau)-(3/ln 2)I(g_tau)].

The cumulative log term remains unpaid universally. Its presence is not an FEI proof.

### 4. Hypothesis with a proved finite influence price

Fix epsilon in (0,1]. Suppose at EVERY live node, every T with b_T^2>0 satisfies theta_T>=epsilon. Zero mismatch packets are exempt. Then lambda_t<=log_2(1/epsilon)d_t. This is a directly checkable spectral density hypothesis, not an assumption that the desired entropy drift is already bounded.

With C_epsilon=log_2(1/epsilon)+3/ln 2, the quantity

    Z_t=C_epsilon I(g_t)-H(g_t)

is a supermartingale: E[Z_{t+1}-Z_t|F_t]=D_t-C_epsilon d_t<=0. Equivalently H(g_t)-C_epsilon I(g_t) is a submartingale. Z_0=C_epsilon I(f)-H(f); at constant leaves Z_tau=0. For arbitrary stopping leaves,

    H(f)<=C_epsilon I(f)+E[H(g_tau)-C_epsilon I(g_tau)].

If terminal functions satisfy H<=C_epsilon I, this proves H(f)<=C_epsilon I(f). The conclusion holds in every dimension for any policy/tree satisfying this same fixed epsilon. No assertion is made that every Boolean function admits such a tree. Parities (queried theta=1) show the hypothesis is nonempty in unbounded dimension. As another simple sufficient condition, if every positive d_t>=delta, then B_t<=h_2(d_t)<=d_t[log_2(1/delta)+1/ln 2], and the same conclusion holds with C_delta=log_2(1/delta)+3/ln 2. These are conditional class statements, not new universal FEI results.

For a general F_t-measurable state potential Q_t, C V_t+Q_t-E_t is a supermartingale exactly when D_t<=C d_t+Q_t-E[Q_{t+1}|F_t]. This specifies the sign of the nonlocal debt needed by A064; it does not construct a universally paid Q.

### 5. Obstruction and first unsupported universal line

B05 gives actual Boolean splits with D>=B and B/d >= (1-2^{-k})(k-2) for every even k>=4. Hence no fixed finite C makes CI(g_t)-H(g_t) a supermartingale for ALL fair policies: start by querying that selector. This consumes the source-bound B05 control, rather than rerunning it or misreading it as failure of existential coordinate selection. The first unsupported universal step is: find an adaptive tree paying E sum lambda_t plus its terminal deficit by a dimension-independent multiple of I(f), or find a nonlocal Q whose boundary and conditional drift achieve that payment. The exact telescope alone does not supply it.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The full proof is saved in POINT_CERTIFICATE.md. Writing d=2^{1-n}, the spectrum has empty mass (1-d)^2 and every nonempty mass d^2. A query has a constant child and a point-function child on n-1 variables. Thus every coordinate has the same rate R_n=(H_n-H_{n-1}/2)/d. The exact closed formula is (3) of that certificate.

The all-dimensional series comparison proves R_n strictly decreases for n>=3 and tends to 4. R_1=0, R_2=4, and the sharp maximum is R_3=12-(9/2)log2 3 in (4.867,4.868), attained exactly at dimension three. This is proved analytically for all n, not extrapolated from a finite table. In particular the dimension-four rate lies in (4.742,4.743), as the lead requested.

The exact one-sided log-charge rate is L_n=1-d+d log2((1-2d+2d^2)/d^2). Consecutive rates obey (9), and their sign is exactly the sign of the polynomial 1-4d. Hence the sharp maximum is L_3=L_4=(3+log2 10)/4 in (1.580,1.581); the tail strictly decreases from dimension four and tends to 1. Direct uniform-nu computation gives KL_2(nu_i||q_i)=n-1-L_n. Thus all coordinates of these rare functions recover their growing rarity logarithm, with a sharp dimension-independent unpaid remainder below 8/5.

All nonconstant physical descendants are point functions, so C I(g_t)-H(g_t) is a supermartingale for every fair adaptive rule in this family exactly at or above the sharp class price C=R_3. At C>=R_3, the lead's minimal nonnegative reserve Q* vanishes everywhere by backward induction. The n=3 node forces sharpness of that drift price. This does not claim that the sharp FEI constant H/I of the class is the same as its sharp drift price.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

1. For block A and residual Fourier index w, let a_{u,w}=fhat(u union w), c_{x,w}=sum_u a_{u,w}chi_u(x), and q_w=sum_u a_{u,w}^2. The actual joint physical/residual experiment has P(X_A=x,W=w)=2^-|A| c_{x,w}^2. Boolean Parseval gives a uniform physical marginal; partial Walsh Parseval gives residual marginal q. The spectral parent conditional law is nu_w(u)=a_{u,w}^2/q_w and the physical posterior is r_w(x)=2^-|A|c_{x,w}^2/q_w. Therefore B_A=sum q H(nu)=H(S_A|S_C), J_A=|A|-sum q H(r)=I(X_A;W), and H(f)-E H(f_x)=B_A+J_A. In the packet's collision notation B_W=B_A and M_W=J_A. Physical outcome entropy |A| is a different quantity.

2. The experiment does not specify how the deleted parent label U is coupled to the branch X_A. Every extension with the correct (U,W) and (X_A,W) marginals has I(U,W;X_A)=J_A+I(U;X_A|W). The canonical A037 lift imposes conditional independence and attains the minimum J_A. The three-bit point defect in PHYSICAL_SPECTRAL_DISTINCTION.md gives two exact nonidentical lifts with unchanged physical/residual marginals; the additional information in the second is strictly positive by nonindependence and Gibbs. This demonstrates why a kernel is required before assigning full-label information.

3. Independently reconstruct A037's finite adaptive common lift. Starting with root S~fhat^2, maintain current S_h=S intersect R_h. At node h draw outcome x with kernel r_{h,w}(x), w=S intersect (R_h\A_h), and erase A_h from the current set. Induction gives actual fair physical branches and actual conditional child spectra. Since the kernel depends on the root S only through w and history, I(S;next outcome|h)=J_h. For stopped transcript L, sum p_h J_h=I(S;L) and H(S|L)=sum p_h B_h+E H(g_L). These are baseline identities already proved by A037 and are independently accepted here at this finite-tree scope. They measure actual information under the stated coupling; they do not erase root posterior uncertainty when current coordinates disappear.

4. New fixed-block coarsening refund. Fix A and query all and only its coordinates, possibly choosing their order from physical history. For deterministic policy the full transcript is in bijection with X_A. The final joint (X_A,S_C) law equals the actual direct-block experiment: each leaf has uniform probability and the actual child spectrum. Under the sequential lift put R_A=I(S_A;X_A|S_C). The chain rule gives sum p_h J_h=I(S;X_A)=J_A+R_A. The total entropy decrement is order independent, so sum p_h B_h=B_A-R_A. Equivalently sum p_h B_h=H(S_A|S_C,X_A). Thus 0<=R_A<=B_A. The direct-block lift has R_A=0 by construction; singleton refinement can reveal erased spectral information and reduce residual erasure. The sum is invariant; its two pieces can depend on query order. This is a conditional-information identity, not an influence-payment theorem.

5. Reference audit. For normalized supported child references Q_x, mixture Q=E Q_x and posterior t_w(x)=2^-a Q_x(w)/Q(w), the joint KL chain rule gives E D(P_x||Q_x)=D(q||Q)+sum q D(r_w||t_w). Moreover sum q D(r_w||t_w)=J_A+E log2(2^-a/t_W(X_A)). The last term is signed and cannot be suppressed unless its cancellation is proved. This is the precise local reference/mixing correction; A037's general channel/reset ledger applies across incompatible node references.

The refund has a sharp quantitative ceiling. The self-contained positive-series proof of h2(t)>=4t(1-t), applied to the erased-bit and branch posteriors in each singleton fiber, gives J_h<=B_h. Hence R_A<=(B_A-J_A)/2. For any canonical singleton stopping tree, I(S;L)<=[H(f)-E H(terminal)]/2 and H(S|L)>=[H(f)+E H(terminal)]/2. Two-bit AND attains the ceiling with direct block charges (2,0), sequential charges (1,1), and refund 1; disjoint AND products show sharpness in arbitrarily large dimensions. Thus paying only released root information leaves at least half the original entropy unpaid. This is a coupling-mechanism barrier, not an FEI refutation.

6. Controls. Isospectral children give J=B=0 even when the physical branch is a fair bit and the functions differ. For nearly identical child squared spectra P_+,P_-, define m=(1-sum sqrt(P_+P_-))/2. The parent minority fiber mass sums to m, so B<=h2(m); the baseline Hellinger inequality gives J<=2m/ln2. Both vanish with m, retaining the logarithmic scale of B. Exact point-defect expressions r=2..8 are preserved by the checker. None of these statements pays a universally large rare-erasure bill by one local influence.

The first unsupported universal line is a dimension-independent bound for H(S|L)=sum p B+E H(terminal), under a constructive query policy whose physical influence is charged once. Paying J again, or dropping its kernel/reference correction, cannot provide that bound. The fixed-block refund identifies a potential mechanism but does not establish sufficient refund on arbitrary Boolean sources.

# complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

## Payment theorem and terminal correction

Let B=E sum d and L_I=E I(terminal) on the same finite tree. If an adapted integrable Q satisfies the displayed payment condition, E Q0<=K B, and

    E[H(terminal)-Q_terminal] <= L L_I,

then

    H(f) <= (C+K) B + L L_I <= max(C+K,L) I(f).

Indeed sum_{s<t}(D_s-Cd_s)+Q_t is a supermartingale. Finite expectation summation gives E sum D<=CB+E Q0-E Q_terminal. Add the retained terminal entropy, and use the exact nonreusing influence split I(f)=B+L_I. The potential may be signed at intermediate nodes. A sufficient leaf condition is Q_terminal>=0 with H(terminal)<=L I(terminal). If the weaker root condition E Q0<=K I(f) is all that is proved, the corresponding conclusion is H<= [K+max(C,L)]I; it does not give the sharper queried-budget constant. This distinction prevents using a terminal influence account once for the reserve and again for the leaf.

For any fixed finite tree define A_v=E[H(terminal)|v], Q_v=H(g_v)-A_v. A is a martingale. Thus Q_v-avg Q_child=D_v, and Q_terminal=0. The erasure plus JS identity makes D_v>=0, so backward induction proves Q_v>=0. The same backward induction shows this is the unique exact-drift solution with zero leaves. Its construction is general, but Q0=H(f)-E H(terminal) is not automatically linearly paid. With complete constant leaves and a universal Q0<=KI, that initial assertion would be FEI itself. No such bound is assumed.

This is a remaining-bill reserve; it need not decrease pathwise. Its entire expected terminal value is exactly zero for the finite trees below. No dimension limit, uniform-integrability shortcut or almost-sure disappearance of unpaid core entropy is invoked.

## Exact spectral minority/KL bill and coherence

At a node let x_T,y_T be the two actual child Fourier coefficients, q_T=(x_T^2+y_T^2)/2, m_T=(|x_T|-|y_T|)^2/4, M=sum m_T, and nu=m/M for M>0. Exactly

    D = M log(1/M) - M KL(nu||q) + R_B + JS(x^2,y^2),
    R_B = sum_T (q_T-m_T) log[q_T/(q_T-m_T)].

Zero-mass terms contribute zero, including M=0. The two remainders satisfy R_B<=M/ln2 and JS<=2M/ln2. The first follows from -(1-t)ln(1-t)<=t; the second follows from the scalar comparison between the JS contribution and half the squared Hellinger distance, as reconstructed in A062 and the source ISO section 3. M<=d, but M need not equal the signed queried mass d. M is also different from the physical output minority eta tested below.

The reserve drift is this entire D. Therefore Q0 equals the physically weighted sum of these exact bills, with each node's mu log(1/mu) and own-reference KL rebate included once. No KL value from one node is credited to another node with a changed reference. Branch probabilities multiply complete bills and are never substituted for spectral packet probabilities.

For the arbitrary-bias activation proof below, coherent constant-frequency terms remain explicit: m^2 log(m^2), a^2 log(a^2), and (1-pa)^2 log((1-pa)^2). They are the actual squared Fourier coefficients after recombination, not entropy of an incoherent label mixture. This includes the requested alpha^2 log(alpha^2) endpoint terms.

## Explicit arbitrary-core activation reserve and initial bound

Let g be any Boolean core, m=Eg, a=1-m in [0,2], r>=1, p=2^-r, and F=1+A_r(g-1) with fresh point controls. Query controls until the first mismatch, or stop at g after r matches. At an active node with s remaining controls, u=2^-s, set

    Q_s = H(1+A_s(g-1)) - u H(g).

All inactive leaves and the final core have Q=0. Conditional survival to the core is u, so this is precisely the general terminal correction. Its drift is D and it is nonnegative. Exclusive queried influence is B_ctrl=rpa, while expected terminal entropy and influence are pH(g), pI(g).

The actual Walsh coefficients give, with 0log0=0,

    Q_r = 2rpa(2-pa) + p m^2 log(m^2)
          -(p-p^2)a^2 log(a^2) -(1-pa)^2 log((1-pa)^2).

This follows by separating nonempty data packets, empty-data nonempty-control packets and the empty coefficient; no mean sign is discarded. The m term is nonpositive. The final term is <=2pa/ln2. For a>=1 the a term is nonpositive; for 0<a<1 it is at most 2pa[a log(1/a)]<=2pa/(e ln2). Therefore

    Q_r <= [4+2(1+1/e)/ln2] rpa < 8 rpa.

The a=0 case is exactly zero. The last strict constant is proved by the rational lower bounds ln2>56/81 from its atanh expansion and e>65/24 from its exponential expansion; 2*(81/56)*(1+24/65)<4. Negative means, m=0, a=2 and the last-layer sign change are all included. This reconstructs A023 section 4, credited as the source direction; it is not a new claim about the activation entropy identity itself.

If g has an independently proved H(g)<=L I(g), payment gives H(F)<=max(8,L)I(F). Without it the exact pH(g) is retained and unpaid. The threshold paper's activation equivalence explains why arbitrary core entropy cannot be dropped merely because p is tiny.

## Both query orders on an unbounded bent-splice family

Let b be any bent function on even k>=4 bits, v any vertex, delta=2^-k, b'=b-2b(v)1_v, and g the fair physical selector between b and b'. Activate g with arbitrary r>=1 fresh controls. This is an unbounded family in both k and r; r=2k with quadratic b and v=0 is B05.

Bent flatness gives I(b)=k/2 and |Eb|=sqrt(delta). Point-flip edge counting gives Ibar=(I(b)+I(b'))/2>=k/2-kdelta>=7k/16; I(g)=Ibar+delta. Also H(g)<=k+1<=5k/4, so H(g)<=20I(g)/7<3I(g). The activation parameter a=1-Eg lies in [11/16,21/16]. Thus control-first has Q0<=8rpa, zero terminal reserve and terminal entropy <=3pI(g), yielding H<=8I.

For selector-first, first query the physical selector at the root, then use the above control-first trees in its two children. Leaves are constant, b or b'. Root d=pdelta. The signed Fourier allocation is lambda=d[log(1/d)-KL(nu||q)]<=d log(1/d); the full decrement is <=lambda+3d/ln2. Therefore

    D_selector <= pdelta(r+k+3/ln2) <= rpa.

For the second bound use delta<=1/16, kdelta<=1/4, r>=1, 1/ln2<81/56, and 1/16+1/4+243/896<11/16<=a. The actual root potential is D_selector+avg(Q_G,Q_H). Child reserves average to <=8rpa, so Q0<=9rpa<=9B, B=rpa+pdelta. The expected terminal entropy is <=pk; its expected influence is pIbar>=7pk/16, so it is separately certified below 3. This yields H<=9I on this order.

The selector bill and descendant control bill receive disjoint allowances of one and eight times B_ctrl, within the declared nine-times reserve. The terminal data account pIbar is separate. Control-first has no independent selector bill and keeps its entire entropy in the core leaf. The terminal correction accounts for this difference exactly. No coordinate's initial influence is silently pledged to two bills without the stated extra factor.

For products of disjoint components the same Q values add: Fourier entropy and influence add, conditional terminal entropy adds, and a query affects only its component. Thus these certificates retain unbounded component count without a depth factor. This extension is elementary tensor additivity, not a solution for shared controls.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

The complete proofs are saved in `DERIVATION.md`. For a physical block B, residual spectral index T, and assignment y, let p_y(T)=hat(f_y)(T)^2 and q_T=E_y p_y(T)=sum_{U subset B}p_{U union T}. Define

M_T=sum_U p_{U union T}ln(q_T/p_{U union T}),
C_T=E_y p_y(T)ln(p_y(T)/q_T).

The usual C006 entropy decrement is M_B+C_B, summing all rows. Remove the empty residual row to obtain M_B^+, C_B^+, and set ell_B=sum_{nonempty U subset B}p_U ln(1/p_U). The exact new heat identity is

2[K(f)-E_y K(f_y)]=M_B^+ + C_B^+ + ell_B.

All three terms are nonnegative, so K decreases in expectation under every physical restriction. This accounts for the constant-mode boundary exactly: ell_B is the information in Fourier coefficients supported wholly inside the erased block, which become constants in the children.

For B={i}, the channel is at most 2 Inf_i(f) nats. Booleanity gives |hat(f)({i})|<=Inf_i(f), hence ell_{ {i} }<= (2/e)Inf_i(f). Both charges are paid using the same queried coordinate; in a stopping tree their cumulative cost is at most (2+2/e)[I(f)-E I(leaf)]. Terminal K and the endpoint constant-mode entropy remain explicit.

Let R_nat(f)=sum_i M_i^+(f). Then 0<=B_nat(f)-R_nat(f)<=(1+2/e)I(f). More decisively, for every arbitrary Boolean core g and m>=1, F_m=y product_j g(x^(j)) satisfies R_nat(F_m)=m B_nat(g) and I(F_m)=mI(g)+1. Therefore a universal R_nat<=A I implies universal B_nat<=A I with the same constant. The optimal uniform constants for the two erasure quantities are equal. C018 consequently gives FEI in bits with constant (A+2)/ln2. No easier universal class has been introduced by deleting the empty row.

# A068 / B14: context-dependent antichains with quadratic spectral fibers

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

Let h:{-1,1}^q -> {-1,1} be regular in the published sense: after fixed coordinate orientations it is monotone and has a total desirability order. Let z consist of m independent uniform bits, write z_j=(-1)^{u_j}, and let Q_1,...,Q_q be arbitrary polynomials of degree at most two over F_2 in u. They may share every control variable. Put a_i(z)=(-1)^{Q_i(u)} and

    F(x,z)=h(x_1 a_1(z),...,x_q a_q(z)).

The x_i are distinct private physical data coordinates, independent of z. For every finite q,m, with no bound on the number, degree of overlap, or rank of the quadratic controls,

    H(F) <= C_reg I_x(F)+2 I_z(F) <= C_reg I(F),
    C_reg=log_2(4+e)+2log_2(e*pi)<8.937.

Here I_x=sum_i Inf_{x_i}, I_z=sum_j Inf_{z_j}; entropy is in bits. The sharper consequence H(F)<=C_reg D_x(F)+2I_z(F), where D_x=sum_i min(Inf_{x_i},1-Inf_{x_i}), follows from the recovered centered regular theorem. The ordinary inequality above is reconstructed with a complete normalized reference below. This is a proper-class result, not full FEI. Its local proof and exact validation are complete; independent acceptance is pending. Novelty outside the read corpus is unverified.

## sources actually read, revisions and theorem locators

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. The replacement pivotal geometry

Fix z and write y_i=x_i a_i(z), also incorporating any fixed orientations of h. The map x -> y is a coordinate orientation, preserving uniform measure. For data pivot x_i,

    d_{x_i} F(x_{-i},z)=a_i(z) d_i h(y_{-i}).

In the coordinates preceding i in h's desirability order, every fixed-z pivotal fiber is therefore an antichain in the orientation a_j(z). The orientation is allowed to depend on the exterior control assignment, but not on the resampled predecessor coordinates. For every resampling mask R, its restricted fiber is still an antichain. Thus the signed relative-noise estimate remains valid after averaging z. This is the precise sufficient condition replacing one globally fixed orientation. It does not imply that F is globally unate.

For rank i, U_i={1,...,i-1} after reordering, the normalized derivative spectrum of F satisfies

    E (1-t)^{|T intersect U_i|} <= E c_B,
    c_b=2^{-b} binom(b,floor(b/2)), B~Bin(i-1,t).

Indeed bound d(X)d(Y) by |d(X)||d(Y)| and, conditionally on X,z,R, bound the latter support probability by c_|R|. Since R is independent of X,z, the derivative mass factors out. Signs of derivatives are harmless. The Fourier partial-noise identity diagonalizes resampling exactly as in the baseline. The same harmonic integral then gives

    E ln[i/(|T intersect U_i|+1)] <= sum_{b=1}^{i-1} c_b/b <= 1+ln 2.

For completeness, E h_kappa = integral_0^1 [1-E(1-t)^kappa] dt/t is at least sum_{b=1}^{i-1}(1-c_b)/b. Also ln[i/(kappa+1)] <= h_{i-1}-h_kappa. Finally c_{2j-1}=c_{2j}=4^{-j}binom(2j,j), and the binomial series yields sum_{j>=1} c_{2j}/(2j-1)=1 and sum_{j>=1} c_{2j}/(2j)=ln 2. This is the recovered sharp rank mean, now applied to conditional orientations.

### 2. Exact data-indexed packets; no incoherent replacement

For S subset [q], let a_S=product_{i in S} a_i, Q_S=sum_{i in S} Q_i over F_2. Expanding h gives the exact identity

    F(x,z)=sum_S hhat(S) chi_S(x) a_S(z),
    Fhat(S,T)=hhat(S) ahat_S(T).

Distinct S have disjoint full Fourier indices because their physical data labels differ. Hence there is no coherent sum to discard. Define p_S=hhat(S)^2 and nu_S(T)=ahat_S(T)^2. Parseval gives sum_T nu_S(T)=1 even when hhat(S)=0. Then

    P_F(S,T)=p_S nu_S(T),
    H(F)=H(h)+sum_S p_S H(a_S),
    I_x(F)=I(h),
    I_z(F)=sum_S p_S I(a_S).

These identities require distinct private data bits. They are valid for arbitrary Boolean controls; the next step uses degree at most two.

### 3. Quadratic control packets are affine flats with a paid rank

Let a(u)=(-1)^{Q(u)} for a polynomial Q of degree at most two on F_2^m. Let B be its alternating polar matrix, so

    Q(u+v)+Q(u)+Q(v)+Q(0)=u^T B v,
    r=rank_F2(B), R=ker(B).

The spectral characteristic function is its physical autocorrelation:

    sum_T ahat(T)^2 (-1)^{T dot v}
       = E_u a(u)a(u+v)
       = 1_{v in R} (-1)^{Q(v)+Q(0)}.

On R, Q(v)+Q(0) is linear because its polarization vanishes. Choose t_0 extending this functional. Walsh inversion gives

    nu(T)=2^{-r} 1_{T in t_0+R_perp}.

Thus nu is uniform on an affine space of dimension r, and H(a)=r. Let J be the coordinate support of the linear space R_perp. Every coordinate in J is uniform on the affine space; the remaining coordinates are fixed. Since dim(R_perp)=r, |J|>=r. Therefore

    I(a)=E_nu |T| >= |J|/2 >= r/2,
    H(a)=r <= 2 I(a).

This includes r=0, affine-linear controls and constant controls: their spectra are single atoms and their entropy is zero. We do not treat a non-Boolean normalized vector as a quadratic phase. The displayed Boolean autocorrelation proves the affine-flat assertion.

For each data set S, write L_S=t_S+ker(B_S)_perp and r_S=rank B_S. The product a_S remains a quadratic phase, so its full entropy bill r_S is paid by twice its physical control influence. The geometry is a family of context-oriented pivotal cubes over the control cube, with affine spectral fibers of possibly different dimensions over data sets.

### 4. Complete normalized rank reference and all its costs

Ranks are relabeled i=1,...,q. On data sets of size k define

    E_k(S)=product_{i in S} i^{-2},
    Z_k=sum_{|S|=k} E_k(S),
    R_k(S)=E_k(S)/Z_k.

Z_k is finite and strictly positive for 0<=k<=q, including Z_0=1. Euler's product from the baseline bounds Z_k<=pi^{2k}/(2k+1)!. Thus, if S={i_1<...<i_k},

    -log_2 R_k(S)
      <= (2/ln 2) sum_{j=1}^k ln(i_j/j)+k log_2(pi^2/4).

The factorial comparison (2k+1)!>=4^k(k!)^2 follows by induction. Define the full conditional reference

    R_k^F(S,T)=R_k(S) 2^{-r_S} 1_{T in L_S}, |S|=k.

For each S, L_S has exactly 2^{r_S} points. Therefore sum_{S,T} R_k^F(S,T)=1. It covers all positive Fourier atoms. Let w_k=P_h(|S|=k) and R^F(S,T)=w_|S| R_|S|^F(S,T). This too is a normalized probability law. Zero w_k levels carry zero actual mass and contribute zero.

The full reference cost is

    log_2(1/w_k) -log_2 R_k(S) + r_S.

In particular, the control geometry is not discarded: its conditional affine rank is charged once per complete Fourier set. The fixed polynomial list and coordinate order are part of the reference instance known to the decoder. Given S, the decoder computes B_S and L_S and decodes an r_S-bit affine coordinate. No extra choice of geometry is made separately for each observed set. If an unknown representation is selected from several lists, a normalized prior and its selection cost would additionally be required; this theorem does not waive that cost.

Gibbs' inequality, the derivative law and Step 1 now give

    H(F) <= H(|S|)+(2/ln 2)(1+ln 2) I_x
                    +log_2(pi^2/4) I_x + E_p r_S.

The spectral-level entropy of h is at most log_2(4+e) I(h)=log_2(4+e) I_x by the recovered Boolean level lemma. Step 3 gives E_p r_S<=2I_z. Consequently

    H(F) <= [log_2(4+e)+2log_2(e*pi)] I_x+2I_z.

This proves the claimed complete rank-reference theorem. Alternatively Step 2 plus H(h)<=C_reg D(h) gives the stated D_x refinement directly. No unsupported line occurs in the class theorem. For arbitrary controls, the first unsupported universal line would instead be sum_S p_S H(a_S)<=K sum_S p_S I(a_S) with absolute K. Taking h to be a dictator reduces that proposed line to full FEI on an arbitrary control a_1; the quadratic hypothesis is essential to the current proof.

# A069 / B14: stable transfer of the percolation mask decoder

Full FEI remains OPEN. This is a complete local derivation for a proper family and an abstract perturbation interface; independent acceptance and supervisor copying are pending. All entropy is in bits.

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

Let g_d be complete depth-d ternary recursive majority on n=3^d independent uniform sign bits, d>=1. For any N>=n, pad g_d with N-n unused bits. For an arbitrary deterministic edit set D in the N-cube, let f=g_d off D and f=-g_d on D, and rho=|D|/2^N. The target proved here is a complete, injective prefix code for every spectral subset, including the empty subset, with:

* H(f)<=E_{S_f} L_T(S_f)<=12 I(f) whenever N rho<=1/8.
* For a single edited input, H(f)<=E_{S_f} L_T(S_f)<=25 I(f), uniformly in d,N and edit location; the constant 12 applies for N>=6.
* Its cost is stable under padding followed by one point flip: for fixed d, the cost difference from the padded base code tends to zero as N tends to infinity.

The abstract hypothesis is a fixed rooted partition tree T with singleton leaves, at most three children per internal vertex, and a paid spectral occupancy sum. Its coordinates and child order are fixed before the sample is drawn. No spatial estimate is assumed. Tree choice may depend on the function, but not on the realized Fourier set.

The source does NOT say that a spectral sample is a deterministic function of a pivotal set, or of a few arms. It decodes the sample from occupied-cell masks. Arm events bound block oscillation probabilities, which bound spectral occupancy. These two steps must be distinguished.

## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

### 1. Abstract all-set decoder and complete cost

For each internal vertex v, let C_v be its cell and b_v its number of children, with 2<=b_v<=3. Encode the empty set by the one-bit word 0. Encode a nonempty set by 1 and, in preorder, encode every occupied internal vertex's nonempty child mask using b_v bits. Number masks 1,...,2^{b_v}-1 and write mask-1 in b_v bits. One word is unused at each vertex. Unoccupied vertices are skipped. At singleton leaves, occupation already identifies the coordinate, so no further bits are needed.

The decoder knows which occupied vertices remain from previously decoded masks. It stops precisely when this list is empty. This proves unique decoding, termination, and prefix freedom. Every subset has a word. Thus Q_T(S)=2^{-L_T(S)} has total mass <=1 by Kraft, with

    L_T(S)=1 + sum_{v internal} b_v 1{S intersects C_v}.

The root bit, all child choices, and all physical coordinate locations are paid: locations are specified by the fixed tree and the decoded masks. There are no latent witnesses, unrevealed leaves, sample-dependent geometry choices, or omitted reference normalizers. The fixed decoder is available for all sets, including those absent from g's spectrum. Gibbs' inequality for the subprobability Q_T gives

    H(f)<=Gamma_T(f):=sum_S fhat(S)^2 L_T(S)
         =1+sum_v b_v P(S_f intersects C_v).                 (1)

Indeed normalize Q_T by its mass Z<=1, use KL>=0, and note that adding log2 Z<=0 can only reduce the cross-entropy bound. This is the integral-bit version of percolation Lemma 2.1. Its abstract influence hypothesis is Gamma_T(f)<=K I(f). Decoding alone never proves that hypothesis.

A tree without unary vertices has at most N-1 internal vertices, since sum_v(b_v-1)=N-1. Therefore

    max_S L_T(S)<=1+3(N-1)=3N-2.                           (2)

### 2. Perturbation transfer, valid without spatial or Boolean spectral assumptions

For Boolean f,g on the same uniform N-cube, put delta=f-g and rho=P(f!=g), so ||delta||_2^2=4rho. For any fixed nonnegative finite cost L, weighted Euclidean Minkowski gives

    sqrt(Gamma_L(f)) <= sqrt(Gamma_L(g))
                        +sqrt(sum_S deltahat(S)^2 L(S))
                     <= sqrt(Gamma_L(g))+2 sqrt(rho max L). (3)

Equivalently, |Gamma_L(f)-Gamma_L(g)| is at most

    4 sqrt(rho max L Gamma_L(g)) + 4rho max L.              (4)

For linear payment one may use (a+b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2 coefficientwise:

    Gamma_T(f)<=2Gamma_T(g)+8rho(3N-2).                    (5)

This retains coherent cross terms; it does not treat squared spectra as an incoherent mixture. The only Boolean input here is ||f-g||_2^2=4rho. The weighted triangle statement itself holds for arbitrary real vectors.

The physical edge events for f and g can differ only if x or x with coordinate i flipped lies in D. Thus

    |Inf_i(f)-Inf_i(g)|<=2rho,
    |I(f)-I(g)|<=2N rho.                                  (6)

For a one-point edit at x0, deltahat(S)=-2g(x0)2^{-N} chi_S(x0) for every S. In particular, for any cell C,

    sum_{S intersects C} deltahat(S)^2
       =4*2^{-N}(1-2^{-|C|}),
    P(S_f intersects C)<=2P(S_g intersects C)
                         +8*2^{-N}(1-2^{-|C|}).           (7)

This directly exhibits stability of the occupancy sum itself, even though the edited Fourier support can become dense.

### 3. Direct nongeometric payment for recursive majority

The three-bit majority gate has the exact Boolean expansion

    Maj3(y1,y2,y3)=(y1+y2+y3-y1*y2*y3)/2.

Its spectral child mask is one of {1},{2},{3},{1,2,3}, each with probability 1/4. At every composition node the child functions are balanced and use disjoint physical blocks. Consequently any output Fourier set has a unique decomposition into its occupied child blocks; substitution multiplies their coefficients with no interference. Conditional on the child mask, their nonempty spectral samples are independent copies of the child law. This follows directly from the expansion and agrees with threshold Proposition 7.1.

An individual child is selected with probability 1/2. Thus any main-tree cell at depth j is occupied with probability 2^{-j}. There are 3^j such cells, so the expected number occupied at that level is (3/2)^j. Singleton leaves yield

    I(g_d)=(3/2)^d,
    E(number of occupied main internal nodes)
       =sum_{j=0}^{d-1}(3/2)^j=2(I(g_d)-1).               (8)

This is the required occupancy growth/payment replacing percolation's arm estimates. It is proved from the named Boolean family, not imported from spatial geometry. The four-mask two-bit code on the unedited support also gives the known identity H(g_d)=4(I(g_d)-1). That support-only code is NOT used after editing.

To code all subsets, use the three-bit masks of section 1. If there are padding bits, attach the main ternary tree and an arbitrary binary tree on all padding bits to a new binary root. Under g_d the main branch is always occupied and the padding branch never is. Write Ig=I(g_d). Exactly,

    Gamma_T(g_d)=1+6(Ig-1)+2*1{N>3^d} <=6Ig-3.            (9)

Combining (5), (6), and (9), for every edit set D,

    H(f)<=Gamma_T(f)
         <=12Ig-6+8rho(3N-2)
         <=12I(f)-6+48N rho-16rho.                        (10)

Hence N rho<=1/8 implies Gamma_T(f)<=12I(f). This proves the sparse-edit theorem for arbitrary edit sets, including highly irregular, nonmonotone edits and all choices of signs inherited from g_d.

For a single point, rho=2^{-N}, N>=3. Since N/2^N<=3/8, (10) gives Gamma_T(f)<=12I(f)+12. Balance of g_d gives Ef=+-2^{1-N}, hence Var(f)=1-4*2^{-2N}>=15/16. Parseval gives I(f)>=Var(f), and consequently

    Gamma_T(f)<= (12+12/(15/16))I(f)
              =(124/5)I(f)<25I(f).                       (11)

For N>=6, N/2^N<=1/8, so the sharper constant 12 follows from (10). No floating-point logarithmic estimate supplies any of these signs.

### 4. Padding stability and scope controls

For fixed d, Gamma_T(g_d) is constant for N>3^d by (9). By (2) and (4), a one-point edit changes that paid cost by at most

    4 sqrt(2^{-N}(3N-2)Gamma_T(g_d))
       +4*2^{-N}(3N-2),                                  (12)

which tends to zero. Influence convergence follows from (6). For completeness, spectral total variation tau<=2 sqrt(2^{-N}) follows by Cauchy-Schwarz applied to (fhat-ghat)(fhat+ghat). A maximal coupling and the conditional entropy chain rule give |H(f)-H(g_d)|<=h2(tau)+tau log2(2^N-1), which also tends to zero. Thus this functional passes the B14 perturbation test in its actual paid domain.

The base recursive-majority family is already covered by read-once composition (threshold Corollary 7.3 and the cited composition literature). Reproving its FEI is NOT a new class advance. The additional deliverable is an all-set hierarchy that remains paid after arbitrary sparse truth-table edits; edits are not assumed to preserve the original read-once representation. We do not claim that this neighborhood theorem has no prior literature overlap. For example, changing Maj3 at the all-positive input makes it non-unate: from that input a single negative input changes output -1 to +1, whereas elsewhere the same coordinate has the original positive majority direction. This edited example lies outside the unate/desirability hypothesis of C001. We make no assertion that every edited member is outside every structured FEI theorem.

The normalized non-Boolean control a(x)=N^{-1/2} sum_i x_i has spectrum uniform on singleton sets and I(a)=1. At N=3^d, the same complete ternary tree has one expected occupied vertex at each internal depth, giving Gamma_T(a)=1+3d. This diverges. The decoder and stability lemmas remain valid; the Boolean-family occupancy payment (8) is the indispensable extra step. There is no extension of (8) from normalization alone. An arbitrary tensor factor is not allowed as an unpaid terminal in the family theorem.

First unsupported universal line: for every Boolean f, choose a bounded-arity fixed partition tree, or a fixed-prior collection of complete tree references, whose full expected code cost is <=K I(f) for one absolute K. This report proves that choice/payment only for the recursive-majority neighborhood above. It neither proves nor disproves that universal statement.

## exact target, quantifiers, hypotheses and units

Target: B09-BIASED-BLOCK-UNCERTAINTY@1 in CLAIM_REGISTRY.json. ## complete derivation or exact first unsupported line

Let m_i=8p_i, w(x)=product_i[m_i if x_i=1 else 8-m_i], and V_S=sum_x f(x)w(x) product_i_in_S(8x_i-m_i). In the orthonormal centered basis phi_i=(x_i-p_i)/sqrt(p_i(1-p_i)), the exact squared coefficient is

This follows by writing each expectation with its physical probability numerator and cancelling the 8 powers in the variance normalization.
